title: An Efficient Sparse Fine-Tuning with Low Quantization Error via Neural Network Pruning
abstract: arXiv:2502.11439v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Fine-tuning is an important step in adapting foundation models such as large language models to downstream tasks. To make this step more accessible to users with limited computational budgets, it is crucial to develop fine-tuning methods that are memory and computationally efficient. Sparse Fine-tuning (SpFT) and Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) are two frameworks that have emerged for addressing this problem and have been adopted widely in practice. In this work, we develop a new SpFT framework, based on ideas from neural network pruning. At a high level, we first identify "important" neurons/nodes using feature importance metrics from network pruning (specifically, we use the structural pruning method), and then perform fine-tuning by restricting to weights involving these neurons. Experiments on common language tasks show our method improves SpFT's memory efficiency by 20-50\% while matching the accuracy of state-of-the-art method

translated_title: 一种通过神经网络剪枝实现的具有低量化误差的高效稀疏微调方法
translated_abstract: 微调是将大型语言模型等基础模型适配到下游任务的重要步骤。为了让计算预算有限的用户更容易完成这一步骤，开发节省内存且计算高效的微调方法至关重要。稀疏微调和低秩适配是为解决这一问题而出现的两种框架，并已在实践中被广泛采用。在本工作中，我们基于神经网络剪枝的思想开发了一种新的稀疏微调框架。总体而言，我们首先使用来自网络剪枝的特征重要性指标（具体而言，我们采用结构化剪枝方法）来识别“重要”的神经元/节点，然后通过仅针对涉及这些神经元的权重进行微调。在常见语言任务上的实验表明，我们的方法将稀疏微调的内存效率提升了20-50%，同时达到了与最先进方法相当的准确率。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于神经网络剪枝思想的新型稀疏微调框架，通过结构化剪枝识别重要神经元并仅微调相关权重，在保持与最先进方法相当准确率的同时，将内存效率提升了20-50%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel sparse fine-tuning framework based on neural network pruning ideas, which identifies important neurons via structural pruning and fine-tunes only the related weights, improving memory efficiency by 20-50% while matching the accuracy of state-of-the-art methods.
